questions.question:
D15 — TODO: check whether any of the 5 IDP calls fetch cacheable metadata (JWKS keys, OIDC discovery)?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-wB30y0 on `main`, TODO proposals after the PLAN.md review.
ELI10: The plan does not say what the five IDP calls are. If one of them fetches the IDP's public signing keys (JWKS) or its discovery document, that data changes rarely and comes with cache headers; fetching it on every token validation is wasted latency and quota. This is medium confidence (5/10): I cannot see the calls, so this is a 'go look' item, not a known bug.
What: enumerate the 5 IDP calls; cache any JWKS/discovery fetch for its max-age with a background refresh. Why: cuts per-validation IDP round trips if such calls exist. Pros: fewer calls per login; less IDP dependence at request time. Cons: key-rotation handling (cache miss on unknown kid) must be correct; may turn out to be zero calls, in which case it is a five-minute investigation. Context: start in AuthBroker.validate; list the five call targets. Depends on: nothing; can run before or after R8.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Skip it and possibly leave 1-2 unnecessary round trips per login; build now and you may add caching for calls that are not cacheable.
Recommendation: A because it is a cheap investigation with a plausible payoff, and its context should not be lost.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: captured for a quick look later vs dropped vs investigated inside this PR.

options.label: A) Add to TODOS.md (recommended)

options.label: B) Skip — not valuable enough

options.label: C) Build it now in this PR
options.description: ✅ Enumerating the five calls is minutes and should happen for R8 anyway; caching JWKS is a well-known pattern (human: ~half day / CC: ~10 min). ✅ Fewer IDP calls per login ships together with the parallelization. ❌ Key-rotation edge cases (unknown kid → refresh → retry) add tests to an already large auth PR.
